coachMessages.text: From lesson 4: Green owns rows 0, 2, 4 in a fresh column (0-indexed). Gray owns rows 1, 3, 5. Gray's natural home is the row directly above Green's.

slides.infoProse:
<board instructions>Show a single empty column (col 3). Mark rows 0, 2, 4 with 'td' overlays labelled 'Green' and rows 1, 3, 5 with 'tg' overlays labelled 'Gray'. All other columns empty. Legend: 'td' = Green's natural rows (0, 2, 4), 'tg' = Gray's natural rows (1, 3, 5).</board instructions>

Recall from lesson 4: in any empty column, Green owns rows 0, 2, 4 (0-indexed) and Gray owns rows 1, 3, 5. Gray's natural home is always the cell directly above Green's natural cell.

This is the foundation of Claimeven: whenever Green plays on their natural even-indexed row, Gray can immediately respond above to lock in Gray's natural odd-indexed row in that column.

coachMessages.text: Green plays col 3 and lands on row 0. Gray responds directly above at row 1. What threat did Gray just neutralise?

slides.infoProse:
<board instructions>Show a position where Green has played col 3 (Green disc at row 0) and Gray has just responded at row 1 in col 3 (Gray disc). Also show a Green horizontal three-in-a-row threat whose completing cell passes through col 3 row 1 — that cell is now occupied by Gray. Mark the Gray disc at row 1 col 3 with a 'tg' overlay ('Claimed'). Mark the Green threat discs with 'win' overlays and draw a visual cross or 'td' through the now-blocked threat cell to show the threat is dead. Legend: 'tg' = Gray's claimed cell, 'win' = Green's threat discs (now neutralised), 'td' = Green's threat cell (claimed by Gray).</board instructions>

Green plays col 3 and lands on row 0 (their natural even row). Gray responds immediately above, claiming row 1 (Gray's natural odd row). A Green horizontal threat whose completing cell passed through row 1 of col 3 is now gone — Gray owns that cell. This is Claimeven: respond above Green's even-row play to neutralise every Green threat that passes through the row above.

coachMessages.text: Gray doesn't need to calculate threats one by one. Every time Green plays on an even row, respond directly above — Green's threat network collapses column by column.

slides.infoProse:
<board instructions>Show a mid-game position where Green has played on row 0 in multiple columns (e.g., cols 0, 2, 3, 4) and Gray has responded directly above in each (Gray discs at row 1 in those same columns). Each column now has a Green-Gray pair at rows 0–1. Mark each Gray row-1 disc with a 'tg' overlay ('Claimed'). Also show one or two Green horizontal threat windows that are neutralised because their completing cells in row 1 are already occupied by Gray. Legend: 'tg' = Gray's claimed cells.</board instructions>

Gray doesn't need to calculate threats one by one. Every time Green plays on an even-indexed row, respond directly above. Green's even-row threat network in every such column is automatically neutralised — Gray claimed the row above, and every threat that passed through those cells is now dead.

This board-wide strategy is Claimeven: a systematic response that collapses Green's threat infrastructure without needing to identify each individual threat.

coachMessages.text: Careful — Claimeven only applies when Green plays on their natural even row. If Green plays on an odd row, responding above puts you on an even row. That's Green's territory.

slides.infoProse:
<board instructions>Show a position where Green has just played on row 1 (an odd-indexed row — not Green's natural even row). If Gray blindly responds 'above' at row 2 (an even-indexed row, Green's natural territory), Gray hands Green a cell on Green's natural row. Mark Green's disc at row 1 with a neutral marker. Mark row 2 above it with 'td' ('Wrong — hands Green an even-row cell'). Then show the correct response: Gray should NOT play directly above here. Legend: 'td' = Row 2 here is Green's natural row — do not play here blindly.</board instructions>

Claimeven only works when Green plays on their natural even-indexed row (0, 2, 4…). If Green plays on an odd-indexed row, responding directly above would place Gray on an even-indexed row — Green's territory. That hands Green a cell on their natural row, which is the opposite of Claimeven.

The rule: check the row Green landed on. If it is even-indexed (0, 2, 4…), respond above. If it is odd-indexed (1, 3, 5…), do not apply Claimeven here — a different strategy applies.

socratic.goalPrompt: Green just played in one column, landing on an even-indexed row. Which column should Gray play to claim the cell directly above and neutralise Green's threat?
socratic._boardInstructions: Show a mid-game board (8–10 discs total) where two columns each have a Red disc on row 0. In col 3, the cell at row 1 directly above Red is empty — this is the valid Claimeven target. In a second column (e.g., col 1), the cell at row 1 above Red is already occupied by Yellow, ruling it out as a Claimeven play. Include a horizontal Red three-in-a-row threat whose completing cell passes through col 3 row 1, making the Claimeven motivation concrete. The student must play col 3 as the only open column where Yellow can claim the row directly above Red's even-row disc.
